audit.title: Audit log
audit.description: Who did what, and when. Records cannot be edited or deleted.
security.title: Security
security.description: Policies that apply to everyone in this organization.
security.requireMfaHint: Everyone must set up an authenticator app before they can use Ieum.
security.appliesNextSignIn: This applies the next time each person signs in. Sessions that are already open keep working.
sso.title: Single sign-on
sso.description: Let people sign in with your company identity provider.
sso.name: Display name
sso.redirectHint: Register this redirect URI with your provider: {uri}
sso.metadataHint: Paste the metadata your provider gives you — we'll read the issuer, sign-in URL and signing certificate from it.
sso.certificatesHint: One per line. Both stay valid while your provider rotates keys.
sso.allowIdpInitiated: Allow sign-in started from the provider
sso.allowIdpInitiatedHint: Off by default: we can't tie such a sign-in to a request we started.
sso.samlRedirectHint: Register this reply URL (ACS) with your provider: {uri}
users.title: People
users.description: Invite people, lock accounts, and require two-factor for individuals.
groups.title: Groups
groups.description: Put people in groups, then give roles to the groups.
groups.name: Group name
groups.managedHint: Your identity provider owns this membership — edit it there. Changes made here would be undone at the next sign-in.
groups.memberCount: {count, plural, =0 {No members} one {# member} other {# members}}
groups.noMembers: Nobody is in this group yet.
groups.deleteWarning: Any roles given to this group are removed with it. People keep the roles they were given directly.
roles.title: Roles and permissions
roles.description: Give roles to people and groups. Permissions come from the role.
roles.name: Role name
roles.grantsAfter: Pick permissions after you create it.
roles.deleteWarning: Everyone holding this role loses the permissions it grants.
roles.builtinHint: Built-in roles are restored from their definition on every deploy, so their permissions can't be changed here. The description and the two-factor requirement can.
roles.assignedTo: {count, plural, =0 {given to nobody} one {given to # principal} other {given to # principals}}
roles.scopedElsewhere: Assign this role from the project or space it applies to.
permission.wiki.page.restrict: Restrict who can read a page
workflows.title: Workflows
workflows.description: The states an issue can be in, and how it moves between them.
workflows.counts: {states, plural, one {# state} other {# states}} · {transitions, plural, one {# transition} other {# transitions}}
workflows.unused: not used by any issue type
workflows.showLabel: Show the states and transitions of {name}
workflows.rules: {conditions, plural, one {# condition} other {# conditions}}, {post, plural, one {# action} other {# actions}}
workflows.readOnlyHint: Workflows can't be edited here yet. Removing a state means deciding where the issues already in it should go, so we'd rather not offer a button that breaks things.
fields.title: Custom fields
fields.description: Extra fields on issues. Values are stored per issue; the definition lives here.
fields.keyHint: Lowercase letters, digits and underscores. You'll use this in queries — it can't be changed later.
fields.name: Label
fields.deleteWarning: {count, plural, =0 {No issue has a value for this field.} one {# issue has a value for this field, and it will be deleted too.} other {# issues have a value for this field, and those values will be deleted too.}}
fields.valueCount: {count, plural, =0 {no values yet} one {# issue has a value} other {# issues have a value}}
fields.limited: limited to a project or type
fields.immutableHint: The key and the type can't be changed — the key is the address of every stored value, and the type decides how those values are read.
